conviction_note: The print turns on whether Chubu raises its FY ordinary guide of 185bn yen toward the 202.3bn IFIS consensus. One approved, sourced positive (Chubu PG's wheeling-revenue revision, +97bn yen a year from 1 Nov, about +40bn of FY26 revenue that the July guide may not include) roughly cancels two negatives: oil running well above the guide's $90 assumption, and the still-unquantified Hamaoka withdrawal. Last year Chubu held a conservative guide at 85% progress and the stock fell 3.2%, so the two outcomes are about equally likely: p_up 50, abs 3.5, impact_sum -0.10.
bar: FY3/2027 ordinary profit: IFIS consensus 202,267m yen against the company guide of 185,000m yen (+9.3%), https://kabuyoho.jp/reportTop?bcode=9502 (consensus as of 2026-10-13 update, page read 2026-10-29). The company publishes no H1 guide, so the bar is the full-year revision. The company guide is from the Q1 presentation, https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260729/140120260729501496.pdf

findings.finding: Chubu Electric Power Grid's revised revenue cap was approved by METI on 2026-09-04 (+137.4bn yen over the period, +97bn yen a year on average for Nov 2026 to Mar 2028). New wheeling tariffs take effect 2026-11-01 (low-voltage 9.13 to 10.76 yen/kWh). That is roughly +40bn yen of FY26 revenue for a PG segment the July guide put at only 30bn yen of ordinary profit (down 18bn on cost inflation). Hokkaido Electric revised its FY ordinary profit up 16bn yen on 2026-09-25 for exactly this item. Chubu has filed no revision since 2026-07-29.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 FY3/2025 (2024-10-29), guide revised up: +3.02% next session. H1 FY3/2026 (2025-10-28), guide held at 85% progress: -3.21%. Q1 FY3/2027 (2026-07-29), first guide set at 185bn: -3.91%. Closes from Yahoo chart, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/9502.T?range=2y&interval=1d
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The approval and tariffs are public, and consensus already sits 9% above the guide, which is what analysts adding this item would look like. Two things are not priced. First, whether the July guide already held it: the Q1 deck names only cost increases for PG, and Hokkaido's July guide did not hold it. Second, whether Chubu books it now or keeps a conservative hold as it did all of last year. If it were fully priced, consensus would sit at or above guide plus ~40bn, about 225bn; it sits at 202.
findings.independence: The tariff schedule filing, https://powergrid.chuden.co.jp/news/press/1218277_3281.html (2026-09-11, same company and same fact). Peer precedent from a different issuer: Hokkaido Electric's revision, https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260925/140120260916537214.pdf (2026-09-25).

findings.finding: Fuel is running well above Chubu's July assumption of crude CIF ~$90/b for the FY. Japan average crude rose from 71,857 yen/kl (Feb-Apr) to 116,407 (May-Jul) and 111,869 (Jun-Aug), and LNG from 87,444 to 106,663 yen/t. Hokkaido now assumes $110/b for the FY and $105 from September. That points to a larger time-lag (期ずれ) loss at Miraiz and JERA than the guide's FY -5bn yen (Q1 alone was -9bn), partly offset by JERA's wholesale-market gains.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY3/2027: time lag swung to a loss (-9bn) and Miraiz fell 76bn yen; the stock fell 3.91% on the release that also set the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Fuel prices are a public series and analysts model the lag, so per LESSONS rule 1 this is sized small. What is not priced is how Chubu nets this against the wheeling gain when it decides whether to revise. If the market had fully discounted a cut, consensus would sit at or below guide, not 9% above it.
findings.independence: Hokkaido Electric's revised assumptions (oil $85 to $110), https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260925/140120260916537243.pdf (2026-09-25), a different issuer and document.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-14 Chubu withdrew its Hamaoka 3 and 4 restart applications after the seismic-data misconduct report. It stated the impact on current and future results is 'undetermined at this time', and the H1 release is the first set of accounts since. On 2026-10-27 Nikkei reported the NRA plans additional inspections within the year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Investigation report received 2026-09-11: -3.58% next session. Withdrawal announced 2026-09-14: +0.14%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock fell 3.6% on the report and has not recovered (2,992 yen on 09-11 against 2,677 now). What is not priced is whether H1 carries any extraordinary loss or cost (impairment, write-off of review-related assets). The company says it intends to refile, which makes an impairment unlikely, so this is sized as a small, skewed one-off below operating income.
findings.independence: Nikkei on the NRA's added inspection, https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOUA27C6S0X21C26A0000000/ (2026-10-27). It is the same underlying matter, so not independent evidence of a loss.

outside_window.finding: NRA additional inspections of Hamaoka within the year, plus Chubu's refiling of the Hamaoka 3/4 applications. Both are regulatory overhangs whose resolution falls after 2026-10-30.
From 2026-11-01 the new wheeling tariffs feed into H2 actual PG earnings. That is booked revenue after the window; the in-window part is only the guide revision, filed above.

baseline_tension: Priced lean +0.17, 5-day run-up +2.4% and +1.3% intraday into the print, margin long crowded at 7.2x. The findings net to roughly zero, so they neither confirm nor fight the tape. The strongest positive the release could carry is a guide raised above 202bn on the wheeling revision plus JERA's wholesale strength, possibly with a dividend lift; I looked for it and found the mechanism (approved tariff) but no company signal. The strongest negative is a conservative hold at 185bn, which cost 3.2% last October.

Rule 2 (check the sign): two negatives and two positives; I wrote the strongest positive into baseline_tension and confirmed I searched for it. No further change.
